A_target.statement:
Let $K$ be a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]], $x_0, \ldots, x_n \in K$ distinct and $y_0, \ldots, y_n \in K$.
Then there is a [[Definition:Unique|unique]] polynomial $p \in K \sqbrk x$ of degree at most $n$ with $\map p {x_i} = y_i$ for all $i$.

B_source.statement:
Let $I_0, \ldots, I_n$ be pairwise [[Definition:Coprime Ideals|coprime ideals]] of a [[Definition:Commutative Ring with Unity|commutative ring with unity]] $R$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle R / \bigcap_i I_i \cong \prod_i R / I_i$

substitutions.the ideals I_i: the ideals generated by x - x_i

object_map.reformulation: Interpolation is the Chinese Remainder Theorem in K[x], with the residue modulo x - x_i read off by evaluation.

validity_conditions: The nodes must be distinct, so that the ideals are coprime.
Uniqueness uses that the product of the x - x_i has degree n + 1.
proof_plan:
Let $I_i = \ideal {x - x_i}$.
For $i \ne j$, $\paren {x - x_i} - \paren {x - x_j} = x_j - x_i$ is a unit, so $I_i + I_j = K \sqbrk x$.

The intersection is $\ideal {\displaystyle \prod_i \paren {x - x_i} }$, generated by a polynomial of degree $n + 1$.
By the [[Factor Theorem]], $K \sqbrk x / I_i \cong K$ via evaluation at $x_i$.
By the source result, $f \mapsto \tuple {\map f {x_0}, \ldots, \map f {x_n} }$ induces an isomorphism $K \sqbrk x / \ideal {\prod_i \paren {x - x_i} } \cong K^{n + 1}$.
